stories.title: Mum's perforated bowel ordeal after scan error
stories.summary: "No-one should have to go through what I did after having a baby," said Natalie after a harrowing post-birth ordeal. On 11 January 2023, she welcomed her baby girl into the world by caesarean section at Birmingham's Good Hope Hospital, but the newborn bliss soon turned sour and she was left needing emergency surgery for a perforated bowel. "I knew something wasn't right after Brooke was born, but it felt like my concerns weren't being taken seriously," the 37-year-old from Solihull said. A University Hospitals Birmingham spokesperson said the Trust "is committed to providing safe, high-quality care" to all patients and to "learning from when things do not go as expected." Just days after the birth, she began to suffer severe pain and swelling in her abdomen but says her symptoms were downplayed. As well as debilitating pain, she also suffered vomiting, which included faecal matter, but on 14 January, doctors misinterpreted her scan as showing temporary slowing of her bowel's movements following surgery, medical negligence lawyers at Irwin Mitchell said. "My condition got worse over several days. Being told I needed emergency surgery is something I'll never forget. I was frightened I might die," the factory worker added. Despite raising concerns, her condition deteriorated and she developed sepsis. On 18 January, she underwent emergency surgery, in which part of her bowel was removed and a stoma fitted. The Trust admitted a breach of duty and that a CT scan carried out four days earlier was incorrectly reported.
